description: A LACITE é uma equipe formada por estudantes apaixonados por tecnologia, inovação e ciência, unidos pelo propósito de desenvolver soluções criativas para desafios reais. Com espírito colaborativo, pensamento estratégico e vontade de transformar ideias em realidade, buscamos representar nossa instituição no NASA Space Apps Challenge, contribuindo com inovação e impacto positivo para a sociedade.
summary: PlanetLog is a geospatial intelligence platform developed to identify, analyze, and compare terrestrial environments that share characteristics similar to those found on the Moon and Mars. Utilizing open-source scientific and geospatial data from NASA and partner institutions, the solution evaluates key parameters such as topography, temperature, water presence, and environmental conditions. Its main objective is to transform complex scientific datasets into accessible, actionable insights that support the discovery of planetary analogs and the preparation for future space exploration missions.
details:
PlanetLog bridges the gap between Earth-based research and deep space exploration by serving as an advanced geospatial intelligence platform. It identifies, analyzes, and compares terrestrial environments that share key geological, mineralogical, and environmental characteristics with the Moon and Mars.

1. What It Does and How It Works

  • Data Integration: Aggregates open-source scientific data, satellite imagery, digital elevation models, and planetary observations from NASA, USGS, and partner institutions.
  • Multidimensional Analysis: Rather than relying on surface appearances, PlanetLog evaluates similarities across eight distinct dimensions: Slope/ topography/geomorphology, temperature/extremes, water/ice/volatiles, wind/dust processes, habitability, subsurface structures, and operational conditions.
  • Explainable Scoring: Computes a transparent similarity index accompanied by data coverage and confidence metrics, explicitly detailing both correspondences and mandatory divergences (such as gravity and atmospheric differences).

2. Benefits and Intended Impact

  • Cost-Effective Testing: Provides researchers, students, and aerospace teams with natural laboratories on Earth (such as the Atacama Desert or volcanic regions) to test equipment, rover mobility, and scientific protocols before deployment.
  • Democratization of Science: Converts complex, fragmented geospatial datasets into accessible, structured insights, enabling broader participation in planetary science.
  • Mission Preparation: Supports the planning of future robotic and human exploration missions by identifying high-fidelity analog sites for specific mission objectives.

3. Technology Stack and Tools

  • Ingestion & Standardization: Python (utilizing GDAL and rasterio) for geospatial data processing; STAC standard for cataloging.
  • Geospatial Storage: PostgreSQL with PostGIS for robust spatial queries, paired with Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs (COG) for raster management.
  • Analysis Engine: Python libraries (NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn) handling metric normalization and dimensional weighting calculations.
  • Interface & Visualization: REST API backend paired with interactive web mapping frameworks (MapLibre GL JS / CesiumJS) for side-by-side terrestrial and planetary comparisons.

4. Creativity and Design Considerations

  • Beyond Visuals: Rejects simple visual matches in favor of rigorous, variable-by-variable scientific comparison.
  • Transparent Limitations: Explicitly surfaces factors that cannot be replicated on Earth—such as atmospheric pressure and reduced gravity—ensuring users understand the exact boundaries of an analog.
  • Purpose-Driven Profiles: Allows users to adjust dimensional weights dynamically depending on whether their focus is astrobiology, rover mobility, or geological mapping.
